speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to help you, I need to ask a few specific questions. How long have these symptoms been present, and do you notice any blood in your urine or pain during urination?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed history; the relief of symptoms upon voiding and the recent painful intercourse suggest a specific etiology. Given the frequency, nocturia, and dysuria, do you have any history of sexual contact with new partners or known STIs, and have you noticed any urethral discharge? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Urine_Culture. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound.

text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Color Clear, pH 6.7, Specific_Gravity 1.010, Protein 1+, Glucose Negative, Ketones Negative, Blood Negative, Nitrite Negative, Leukocyte Esterase Negative, WBC 0/hpf, Squamous Epithelial Cells 2/hpf, Bacteria None. Pelvic_Ultrasound: Postvoid_Residual_Urine 25 mL.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for providing those results; the negative urinalysis and ultrasound make a urinary tract infection or structural abnormality unlikely. Given your age, the 5-month history of symptoms relieved by voiding, and dyspareunia, are you currently menopausal, and do you have a history of interstitial cystitis or similar bladder pain syndromes? REQUEST TEST: Cystoscopy with hydrodistention.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Cystoscopy: Normal urethra and bladder mucosa

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the cystoscopy, urinalysis, and ultrasound are all normal, we have effectively ruled out infection, structural abnormalities, and Hunner lesions. Given your age, the 5-month duration of pain relieved by voiding, and the associated dyspareunia, do you have any history of vulvodynia or pelvic floor muscle tension?

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the normal cystoscopy, negative infection workup, and your history of pain relieved by voiding alongside dyspareunia, it is highly suggestive of a pelvic floor dysfunction. Do you report any sensation of tightness or inability to fully relax your pelvic muscles, or do you have difficulty passing gas? REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Floor_Assessment.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Floor Dysfunction (specifically Pelvic Floor Hypertonicity)
